D.treatment: Python and Jupyter Notebook data-analysis module

O.outcome_detail: views of the importance of computational skills

cells.quote: It is remarkable that students' already positive views on the importance of computational skills not only remained consistent but even improved between the pre-survey and the post-survey (see figure 2).
cells.note: The study used matched pre- and post-course surveys; there was no separate control group.

D.treatment: second experiment after additional Python practice
D.comparison: first experiment after the introductory Python sessions

O.outcome_detail: use of Python and Jupyter Notebooks for data analysis

cells.quote: Even if the use of Python and JN was not mandatory, 83% of student groups used Python and JNs for their data analysis in the first experiment and 100% in the second experiment. These results indicate an increase in students’ confidence and proficiency in using these tools.
cells.note: This was an observational comparison of successive laboratory experiments, not a randomized comparison.

D.treatment: Python and Jupyter Notebooks in LAB2
D.comparison: Python and Jupyter Notebooks in LAB1

cells.quote: Our analysis of students’ laboratory notebooks revealed an upsurge in Python and JN utilisation, as illustrated in figure 4 (LAB1 and LAB2). The assessments indicate proficient use of Python in data analysis, with commendable scores in both ’Implement’ and ’Communicate’ categories. Notably, a progression in skill mastery is observed from LAB1 to LAB2.
cells.note: The study reports progression but does not provide a randomized comparison, printed effect size, or statistical test.

D.treatment: Python and Jupyter Notebooks in LAB2
D.comparison: Python and Jupyter Notebooks in LAB1

O.outcome_detail: Optional Python and Jupyter Notebook adoption across laboratory activities

cells.quote: Python and JN, while optional, were increasingly adopted by students, evident from 83% usage in LAB1 to complete adoption in LAB2.
cells.note: The percentages are reported for group submissions and are not presented with uncertainty or a formal significance test.

D.treatment: Jupyter Notebook review exercises at the beginning of the second semester

O.outcome_detail: Retention of Implement and Communicate skills after a three-month break

cells.quote: The analysis shows that about 83% of the groups scored 2 or 3 in both ’Implement’ and ’Communicate,’ showing that students’ mastery of the skills imparted in the previous semester lasted over the break.
cells.note: The study reports retention descriptively but does not provide a directly comparable pre-break percentage or a formal retention test.
